Ways to work

From Slack

An optional listener that lets you type a few commands into one Slack channel. It is off by default, and the Slack-side setup is entirely manual.

In plain words

If your team lives in Slack, you can type short commands in one channel to see drift, list open units of work, rebase a branch or check a merge. A small program on your machine listens and answers. Sigma does not create the Slack app, issue the token or keep the program running for you. A person with access to your Slack workspace does that once.

Commands

CommandWhat it doesKind
--helpLists every command.read-only
--driftRuns a drift-watch sweep on demand.read-only
--list [page]Lists open units of work, ten per page.read-only
--rebase <name>Rebases the unit onto the base branch and pushes it, in an isolated worktree. On a real conflict it reports the files and stops; it never resolves or force-pushes.acts
--merge <name>Runs verify.command against an ephemeral checkout of the unit's remote tip and reports. It never lands anything.acts
--unsafe-merge <name>The same check, then lands the unit at once. It skips only the confirmation a person would answer; a failing verify still blocks it.acts, lands

Mentioning the bot (@your-bot --help) gives the same reply. Slash commands are not supported, on purpose: a slash command can be typed from any channel, and the channel is the only authorisation there is.

The acting commands take noticeably longer than the read-only ones and claim the unit meanwhile; a second command on the same unit gets "already in progress".

What is manual

All of the following is done by a person, once. Sigma does not do any of it for you.

  1. Open the Slack app

    Reuse the app the drift watcher already posts through; no second app is needed.

  2. Turn on Socket Mode

    Generate an app-level token with the connections:write scope.

  3. Add scopes and events

    chat:write, plus channels:history (or groups:history for a private channel); subscribe to message.channels (or message.groups), and app_mention if you want mentions. Reinstall the app to the workspace.

  4. Pick a channel and invite the bot

    Use a channel dedicated to this. Copy its id (shaped like C0123456789), not its name.

  5. Set the secrets in the environment

    SIGMA_SLACK_BOT_SOCKET_TOKEN for the app-level token; the existing SIGMA_SLACK_BOT_TOKEN is reused. Never put either in config.json, which is committed.

  6. Install the dependency

    pip install "slack_sdk[socket-mode]" on each machine that runs the listener. Python's standard library has no websocket client, so this is the one non-standard-library dependency.

  7. Configure the repository

    Set slack_commands.enabled to true and slack_commands.channel_id to your channel id in .sdlc/config.json. For the acting commands to report a real outcome, also set ledger.enabled to true; with it off, a successful rebase or merge is reported as unclear.

"slack_commands": {
  "enabled": true,
  "channel_id": "C0123456789",
  "app_token_env": "SIGMA_SLACK_BOT_SOCKET_TOKEN",
  "bot_token_env": "SIGMA_SLACK_BOT_TOKEN"
}

Running it

You want toDo this
Start it, or restart it if it died/sigma-slack and ask to start it. Safe to run any time: it starts the listener if none is running, replaces a dead one, and touches nothing if one is live.
Check itAsk /sigma-slack for status: running, not running, DEAD, MISCONFIGURED or disabled. /sigma-doctor reports the same liveness.
Stop ittouch .sdlc/state/slack-commands.stop. It disconnects cleanly and removes its own markers.
Test itType --help in the channel. A reply within a few seconds means it is wired up.
Nothing keeps it alive for you

The listener is not started by the loop and is not restarted after a crash or a reboot. A start command only acts when something invokes it. If you want it kept alive, put the start command on a schedule (a launchd or systemd timer, or cron) or run it under a supervisor. The guide has a worked launchd and systemd example; it is one disclosed choice, not a requirement, and a tmux session you restart by hand is also valid for one operator.

Who may command it

Authorisation is channel membership and nothing else: a message is a command if and only if it arrived on the configured channel. There is no per-user allowlist. Keep the channel small. With unit upkeep off, any non-bot message in that channel can land a unit through --unsafe-merge with no further approval; with upkeep on, landing goes through the landing engine and needs a local single-use approval first. The threat model rates this a medium residual risk.

Technical detail

The listener holds a Socket Mode websocket open, so no public URL, tunnel or webhook server is needed. Slack's reconnect and keepalive are handled by the SDK. A single-instance guard stops two listeners running against one .sdlc, and a stale lock from a crash is reclaimed automatically. Liveness is the heartbeat file's age, not the process: doctor separates never run, dead and stale. Not measured here: this site did not run the listener against a live workspace; the guide describes a deployed single-app setup. Auto-start on every loop trigger is recorded as an open design question. Full guide: the Slack commands guide next to the loop skill in the repository; privacy destinations are in privacy.
